samples.summary: `showAuthors` fallback comment names a consumer that does not mount `NotesView`; the fallback is now unreachable
samples.evidence: The new prop doc says the stored-preference fallback is "kept for a mount that owns no view menu (the revision preview)". The revision preview does not mount `NotesView` at all — it mounts the engine directly: `packages/frontend/src/components/history/revision-preview.tsx:758-759` (`new MemNoteStore(text)` + `initializeNote(container, store, resolvedTheme, true, 'view')`). After this change both remaining `NotesView` callers pass `showAuthors` explicitly (`packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-detail.tsx:323`, `packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-notes-layout.tsx:122`), so `storedShowAuthors` / `readShowAuthors()` inside `notes-view.tsx:109` is dead and the comment documents a nonexistent mount.

samples.summary: Share-link note mount hands the notes engine a docs uploader that rejects instead of resolving `null`, so a failed image upload is silent
samples.evidence: `shareTokenImageUploader` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/image-insert.ts:40-49) is a `DocsImageUpload` that throws/rejects on failure. The notes contract is different: `packages/notes/src/view/image-upload.ts:26` types `UploadImage` as resolving `string | null` where `null` means "failed and already reported to the user", and the engine's rejection path only does `console.error('Image upload failed', err)` and drops the ghost (packages/notes/src/view/image-upload.ts:179-190, 199). The workspace mount honours that contract with a toast (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-detail.tsx:203-224). So on a share link an editor-role visitor whose upload fails sees the placeholder vanish with no message.

samples.summary: `readOnlyNoteStore` silently neuters `setLocalSelection`, so an out-of-diff consumer stops publishing viewer carets to peers
samples.evidence: `remote-selection.ts:170/172` calls `this.store.setLocalSelection(...)` unconditionally for every mount; with the new wrapper that call is the shared `noop` on a read-only mount (packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:~150). Before this change a viewer-role share-link visitor (and the read-only revision/preview mounts) published their selection, so collaborators could see where a viewer was reading. That presence is now gone with no code change at the consumer. It appears intentional (docs/design/notes/notes.md:288 says the selection publish is closed at the store), but the behaviour change lands entirely in a module the diff does not touch.

samples.summary: Store guarding is decided once per `[didMount, doc]` effect, so a `readOnly` flip does not re-derive the handle
samples.evidence: The effect that builds `raw`/`store` and calls `initialize(...)` has deps `[didMount, doc]` (notes-view.tsx:174) with an eslint-disable for exhaustive-deps. If any caller ever renders `NotesView` with `readOnly` flipping without a new `doc` (both current callers derive it from a value fixed for the mount — `notes-detail.tsx:319`, `shared-notes-layout.tsx:116`), the mount keeps the stale handle: true→false leaves a write-neutered store whose edits silently vanish, false→true leaves an unguarded one. Worth pinning with a `key` or by adding `readOnly` to the deps so the invariant does not depend on every future caller keeping the prop constant.

samples.summary: `notes-settings` doc comment still says the shared viewer does not use these preferences, which this change makes false
samples.evidence: notes-settings.ts:5-8: "The owner editor (NotesDetail) reads them on open and writes them on change; the read-only shared viewer does not use them." The new share-link layout now reads all three (`readViewMode`, `readKeymap`, `readShowAuthors`) for both roles — packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-notes-layout.tsx:8-12, 47-52 — so the module's stated consumer set is out of step.

samples.summary: `ensureText(doc)` still writes through the raw Yorkie handle, so the "nothing this component can be handed is a writable handle" claim over-states the new boundary
samples.evidence: The new comment at notes-view.tsx:141-150 asserts nothing this component holds is writable on a viewer mount, but the component still holds the raw `doc` from `useDocument()` (notes-view.tsx:125) and `ensureText` calls `doc.update((r) => { r.content = new Text(); })` (notes-view.tsx:83), gated only by the same `readOnly` boolean at line 139 — not by `readOnlyNoteStore`. The store wrapper therefore does not cover this path; a mount that omits/mis-derives `readOnly` writes to the CRDT before any store exists.
